acceptanceCriteria: After a no-progress session on a ticket, the next session's prompt carries a bounded carry-over block holding the prior final-message tail and end reason, labelled untrusted prior-session output; a test proves the block's presence, its bound and its label
Per-role configuration covers on/off, maximum size and number of prior sessions, with defaults recorded in the owning spec under new numbered requirements
Carry-over sessions are distinguishable in dispatch events so progress rates with and without carry-over can be compared; a test covers the event field
No carry-over is injected after a session that recorded progress, or for a different ticket
body: GitHub issue #1122. When a worker session exits at the context handoff threshold with no recorded progress, the dispatcher records its final assistant message in the finished event, but the next session on the same ticket starts from the same prompt without it, rediscovers the same plan and exits again (observed: 13 of 16 no-progress sessions in one program ended at handoff before any edit; three consecutive sessions on one ticket repeated the plan until the stall hold parked it). Expected: a bounded, untrusted carry-over block (tail of the prior final message plus the end reason: handoff threshold, hard stop, tool-call cap) is injected into the next session's prompt for that ticket. Related #1109 (hard-stop salvage), now in batch #1120.
title: dispatch: carry a no-progress session's final message into the next session on the same ticket (#1122)
